It is a letter from the same President to the same congressional recipients, dated one day earlier, and follows the same concrete sequence: transmit proposed legislation; connect it to the President's February 2 message; urge prompt consideration; describe the affected workers and quantitative benefits; explain the broader economic and humanitarian need; and close by identifying an enclosed letter from the Secretary of Labor. C17 and C14 share the general bill-transmittal form, but their overlap is less distinctive and lacks C04's close sequence and same-administration details.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I am transmitting herewith a draft of a bill ... It is designed to carry out a recommendation contained in my message on February 2 to the Congress.","parent_excerpt":"I am transmitting herewith two bills ... I recommended such legislation on February 2 as a part of this administration's program for economic recovery and growth.","explanation":"Both open by transmitting draft legislation and explicitly tie it to recommendations made in the same February 2 message."},{"child_excerpt":"This bill provides needed improvements ... and I urge its prompt consideration.","parent_excerpt":"The need for prompt enactment of this legislation is clear.","explanation":"Both immediately press Congress for prompt action on the transmitted legislation."},{"child_excerpt":"The bill would bring within its protection 4 3/10 million additional workers and would increase the minimum hourly rate ...","parent_excerpt":"The extension of the unemployment compensation program will permit 3 million workers to receive benefits totalling about $950 million.","explanation":"Both quantify the workers who would benefit and summarize the legislation's principal economic effect."},{"child_excerpt":"Our nation can ill afford to tolerate the growth of an under-privileged and underpaid class. Substandard wages lead necessarily to substandard living conditions, hardship and distress.","parent_excerpt":"This has a serious impact not only on the worker and his family, but on the economic health of the entire economy.","explanation":"Both move from the bill's mechanics to the hardship imposed on workers and families and its broader national economic consequences."},{"child_excerpt":"I am also enclosing the letter I received from the Secretary of Labor commenting briefly upon the provisions in the draft bill.","parent_excerpt":"The enclosed letters from the Secretary of Labor and the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare describe the legislation in more detail.","explanation":"Both close by directing the recipients to an enclosed Secretary of Labor letter explaining the proposed legislation."}]}
